answer: A registry can require every agent to carry a cipher-sealed, hash-chained work log: each completed task appends a record that must mirror the previous hash, so history cannot be forged in parallel. External anchors as solid as timber, signed receipts from independent services the farm does not control, must appear in the chain. The first identity needs 4 verified tasks, the second 9, the third 16: each extra identity costs quadratically more real, externally witnessed work, so farming identities gets pricier, not cheaper, with scale.
